title: Rome’s Trevi Fountain sits low because its water comes from a low Roman aqueduct of 19 BC
body: The Trevi Fountain is the show end of the **Aqua Virgo**, the aqueduct that Marcus Agrippa, general of Emperor Augustus, brought into Rome on 9 June 19 BC, according to the Roman writer Frontinus. Its springs at Salone, about 10 km outside the city, lie only about 24 m above sea level, and its channel, almost all of it underground, falls only a few metres in some 21 km, so, as [David Karmon explains](https://waters.iath.virginia.edu/Journal3KarmonNew.pdf), it could reach only the low parts of Rome. Water in a pipe rises no higher than the level it comes from, so fountains on this aqueduct cannot throw tall jets. Pietro Bernini’s Barcaccia at the foot of the Spanish Steps (1626–29) sits below the street, and the architect Nicola Salvi sank the Trevi (1732–62) into the ground, letting its water tumble over carved rocks into a low pool. The same water still feeds the Barcaccia and Gian Lorenzo Bernini’s Fountain of the Four Rivers in Piazza Navona. The coins thrown into the Trevi go to the Catholic charity Caritas: over 1.4 million euros in 2022.

slides.question: The Barcaccia, a boat-shaped fountain at Rome’s Spanish Steps, sits below street level. Why?
options: Its aqueduct’s water had little pressure
To keep it safe from Tiber floods
To hide it from the papal palace
Its stone was too heavy to raise
slides.explanation: Its water comes from the Aqua Virgo, whose low springs leave too little pressure for jets or cascades, so Pietro Bernini set the fountain below the street.

slides.alt: Animation in night teal and travertine: the Trevi Fountain with its pool below the street; the Aqua Virgo’s long profile from low springs, 21 km, 91% underground; a pipe whose water stops at the springs’ level; the sunk Barcaccia; the Trevi’s tumbling water; coins for Caritas.

slides.prompt: The aqueduct’s water stands only half a metre above the street. Sink the fountain until its jet is at least 2 m tall.
slides.takeaway: Sinking the nozzle 1.5 m gives a 2 m jet, yet its top still only reaches the water’s own level. That is why the Barcaccia and the Trevi sit below the street.

slides.alt: The Trevi Fountain by day: the statue of Oceanus in a central arch of the palace front, water spilling over carved rocks into a pale green pool.

slides.label: of the Aqua Virgo ran underground
slides.text: 12,865 of its 14,105 paces, about 21 km, by the figures of the Roman writer Frontinus. Only the last stretch, in the city, ran above ground, partly on arches.

slides.heading: How a low spring shapes a fountain

slides.label: in coins from the Trevi Fountain went to Caritas in 2022
slides.text: Over 33 tonnes of coins, collected from the basin and counted by Caritas di Roma, the Catholic charity, for its work with people in poverty.

slides.question: Without a pump, what sets the highest point a fountain’s water can reach?
options: The level its water comes from
slides.explanation: Water in a pipe rises no higher than its source, less a little for friction. The Aqua Virgo’s low springs leave little height, so its fountains sit low.
